outcome: mode of delivery (normal vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
newborn admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: Fifty women with minor b-thalassemia attending an antenatal care clinic in Azadi Teaching Hospital, Iraqi Kurdistan.
finding: The study found that 14.3% of newborns were admitted to the NICU, and these neonates had lower Apgar scores compared to those not admitted, while their mothers had a higher prevalence of previous dead baby, previous preeclampsia, and were more likely to have undergone a cesarean section.
mod_finding: Most patients (80.0%) underwent a trial of normal vaginal delivery, but mothers of neonates admitted to the NICU were more likely to have undergone a cesarean section (71.4%).
followup_time: Up to delivery, with immediate post-delivery observations for newborns (e.g., Apgar at 1 and 5 minutes, newborn death at 5 minutes).
